We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse structure: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis. The hints: step 1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So likely the final step is coupling of carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need to break the amide bond to give acid and aniline.

Step 2: Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. So we need to break the C=C double bond and the carboxylate to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So retrosynthesis: break the C=C and the acid to give aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or maybe just malonic acid). So we can propose that the unsaturated acid precursor is formed from p-hydroxy? Wait the aldehyde is attached to phenyl ring (the second phenyl). The target has phenyl with substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the aldehyde precursor would be the phenyl with CHO at that position (i.e., 4-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde). So we need to identify that.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine to give sulfonamide. So we can break the S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and the aniline (the p-tolyl amine). Actually the sulfonamide is between p-tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break S-N to give p-toluidine (or its protected form) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the second phenyl sulfonyl chloride). So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the phenyl ring (maybe via chlorosulfonation of the phenyl). That's a forward reaction: aromatic sulfonyl chloride formation from aromatic ring + SO2Cl2. That's not given but we can still propose.

But we need only 3 reactions total. So we can combine steps: 1) amide coupling, 2) Doebner modification, 3) sulfonamide formation. That's three steps.

Thus retrosynthetic tree: target molecule -> (reaction 1) break amide: gives unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) attached to phenyl-sulfonamide? Wait the amide is between the unsaturated acid carbonyl and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So after breaking, we get the unsaturated acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid still has the sulfonamide attached to the phenyl (the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So the unsaturated acid still contains the sulfonamide moiety (the S-N bond). So after step 1, we have two fragments: fragment A: the unsaturated acid with sulfonamide (i.e., Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1). Fragment B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: break the C=C double bond and the acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid. So fragment A becomes aldehyde (aryl-CHO) attached to sulfonamide (still). So we get aldehyde fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (p-tolyl sulfonyl attached to phenyl aldehyde). And malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) as separate reagent.

Step 3: break sulfonamide to give p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the phenyl sulfonyl chloride). So aldehyde fragment splits into p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=O? Wait the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl that also has sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl). In the aldehyde fragment, the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl). Wait need to visualize: original target: p-tolyl-N-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the sulfonamide is between p-tolyl amine and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). So after breaking amide, we have p-tolyl-N-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH. After Doebner, we have p-tolyl-N-SO2-Ph-CHO. After sulfonamide cleavage, we get p-toluidine (p-tolyl-NH2) and phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ph-SO2Cl) with aldehyde? Wait the sulfonyl chloride would be attached to the phenyl that also has aldehyde substituent. So the fragment becomes 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That's plausible.

Thus final three steps: (1) amide coupling, (2) Doebner modification, (3) sulfonamide formation.
